scope: The present Israel Museum campus exterior in Jerusalem, including the original terraced gallery pavilions, 2010 visitor circulation pavilions, named northern pavilion and Shrine of the Book with its pool and basalt wall.

imageryScreen.firstConsulted: Qualla’s local original inventory and source records

selected.title: The Shrine of the Book (Dead Sea Scrolls)
selected.author: Gary Todd
selected.observation: Low white tiled shell on a circular plinth with flared shoulders, a narrow cylindrical crown and an open top. Rectangular stone cooling basin surrounds the shell.

sources.use: Both the layout and surviving stone of the 1965 campus, and the new entrance, passage and ticket pavilion in the 2010 renovation.
Exterior glazing, structural mushroom columns and cantilevered roofs in the archaeology wing.
The design team’s written account of screened glass circulation pavilions.
The design team’s described reuse of the original 11.2 m module.
Kiesler’s 1965 architect account documents the double-parabolic shell, square pool, 6 ft 3 in opening, and basalt wall dimensions. Text only.
The museum exhibit records the standing Shrine design and identities of the architects.

next: Build and validate the hillside galleries, louvered circulation pavilions and Shrine shell on the fixed site frame.
